turn_text: Yeah, so I met with a bunch of farmers today out at the Sangamon County Farm Bureau, had a great group out there. And I will just say this, Jim, there is a lot of anxiety and stress in the Ag community right now because the Ag economy is hurting. Wall Street Journal did an article in January. Ag economy is down about 13% over last year as a direct result of tariffs and retaliation by China. Remember, 25% of the corn and soybeans grown in Sangamon County go to China. We export those. So it's important that we resolve this trade war with China. And I will tell you, I'm not a fan of tariffs, Jim. Tariffs are taxes. They're taxes on consumers. And I've never been a fan. And the retaliation that China has engaged with has hurt our prices. But I will give President Trump credit. I think his implementation of tariffs in a narrowly tailored way has brought the Chinese to the table. China has been ripping us off for 25 years, particularly in the technology space. And technology is the future of this country. forced technology transfers, stealing of intellectual property, theft of our cloud services. We have to hold the Chinese accountable, and so the President has used tariffs to bring them to the table. It has arguably hurt their economy, their stock market is down, but we are at a critical point now in our negotiations, and we need to get our the trade war resolved, but we also have to have an enforcement mechanism in place that causes the Chinese to not continue to engage in the cyber theft and the cyber activities that they've been engaged in. That's really what we're trying to change. Unfortunately, AG is a pawn in this trade war, and sooner rather than later, we need to resolve it. We cannot be in a trade war a year from now or two years from now. I'm optimistic that our trade negotiator, Ambassador Lighthizer, Secretary Mnuchin, they're meeting with the Chinese today. President Trump met with the Chinese trade negotiator yesterday. I'm optimistic that we will get a trade deal here before too long.
